title: ML system design | MLOps & production ML
objectives: Run a structured 45-minute ML system design interview. Know what it takes to keep models alive in production.
exercise: Do two timed (45-minute) ML system design mocks: one classical (merchant fraud scoring) and one GenAI (customer-support assistant). Wrap your Week 8 fine-tuned classifier with MLflow tracking and a simple drift check.
resources: Chip Huyen, Designing Machine Learning Systems (O'Reilly, 2022) and her free ML systems design booklet
Alex Xu, Machine Learning System Design Interview
AI Engineering, Ch. 9–10 (inference optimisation, architecture, user feedback)
DeepLearning.AI short courses on LLM inference

cards.q: Order the 8 ML system design steps.
First thing to do in an ML design interview?
choices: Clarify the business objective, scale, latency and constraints

cards.q: Why propose a simple baseline (heuristic or logistic regression) first?
choices: It sets a bar, ships fast, and reveals data/infra issues before complex models

cards.q: 'Cold start' in system design refers to…
choices: New users/items with no history to base predictions on

cards.q: A fairness consideration for a credit model design?
choices: Check performance and error rates across protected groups; avoid proxies for protected attributes

cards.q: Offline AUC improved but the online A/B is flat. List three causes.
cards.answer: 1) The offline metric doesn't reflect the business metric (better ranking where it doesn't matter, e.g. below the fold). 2) Training–serving skew or feature differences in production. 3) Offline data bias / feedback loop (logged data only covers what the old model showed). 4) The test is underpowered or too short. 5) Saturation: the decision threshold or UI limits the impact. 6) Latency increase offsets gains.
rubric: Any three of: metric mismatch, skew, logging/selection bias, underpowered test, threshold/UI saturation, latency

cards.q: For a ranking model, a better offline metric than AUC is often…
choices: NDCG@k or recall@k for the positions users actually see

cards.q: Why is logged data from the current model biased for training the next one?
choices: It only contains outcomes for items/actions the old model chose (selection bias)

cards.q: A fraud model's offline precision is great, but online the review team is overwhelmed. Likely cause?
choices: Threshold/base-rate differences in production (prevalence shifted) or the offline set wasn't representative

cards.q: Interleaving experiments in ranking are useful because…
choices: They compare two rankers in the same result list, needing far less traffic than A/B

cards.q: Give an example of skew from computing a feature differently in batch vs real time.
cards.answer: Example: 'transactions in the last 24h' computed in batch training from a complete, deduplicated warehouse table (including late-arriving events), but in real time from a stream that misses late events or uses a different timezone or window boundary. Production values are systematically lower and the model under-predicts risk.
rubric: Concrete difference (late events, timezone, window, dedup)

cards.q: A feature store helps prevent skew by…
choices: Defining a feature once and serving the same logic offline (training) and online (inference)

cards.q: A point-in-time correct join ensures…
choices: Each training example only uses feature values available at its prediction timestamp (no future leakage)

cards.q: Best way to detect skew after launch?
choices: Log the features used at serving time and compare their distributions to the training features

cards.q: Batch vs online prediction: choose online when…
choices: Predictions depend on fresh context (current cart, location) and must be returned in real time
You want the lowest cost always

cards.q: What labels, features and offline metric would you use for Grab ETA?
cards.answer: Label: actual trip duration (pickup→drop-off, or driver arrival time), cleaned of cancelled and anomalous trips. Features: route distance, historical and real-time traffic/speeds by road segment, time of day/weekday, weather, pickup/drop-off zones, driver/vehicle type, events. Offline metric: MAE / MAPE, plus a percentile error (p90) and calibration of over- vs under-estimates, sliced by city and hour.
rubric: MAE/MAPE plus tail or asymmetric error, sliced

cards.q: Why might an asymmetric loss suit ETA?
choices: Under-estimating (arriving late vs promise) hurts trust more than over-estimating

cards.q: Good online metric for an ETA model A/B test?
choices: Booking conversion and late-arrival complaints/cancellations, plus actual vs promised error

cards.q: Latency constraint for ETA at booking time implies…
choices: Precomputed segment features plus a light model serving in milliseconds
A large LLM call per request

cards.q: Feedback loop specific to ETA?
choices: Displayed ETAs change rider and driver behaviour (e.g. cancellations), which changes future labels
Traffic depends only on the model

cards.q: The input distribution is unchanged, but fraud patterns change. Which drift is it?
A new marketing campaign brings many younger users; the fraud relationship is the same. Which drift?
Common statistic to monitor feature distribution drift?
choices: Population Stability Index (PSI) or KS test vs a training reference

cards.q: Drift alert fires on a feature. Before retraining you should…
choices: Check for upstream data/pipeline bugs and whether model performance (or proxies) actually degraded

cards.q: Label shift means…
choices: P(y) changes while P(x|y) stays the same (e.g. fraud prevalence doubles)

cards.q: What must you version to reproduce a model?
cards.answer: Data (snapshot or query plus timestamp), code (git commit), config/hyperparameters (and random seeds), and environment (library versions, container image). Also the feature definitions and the trained artefact.

cards.q: What does an experiment tracker (MLflow/W&B) record?
choices: Params, metrics, artefacts and code version per run, so runs can be compared

cards.q: A model registry provides…
choices: Versioned models with stages (staging/production), lineage and approval/rollback

cards.q: CI/CD for models should gate deployment on…
choices: Automated tests: data validation, eval metrics vs the current production model, and latency checks

cards.q: Shadow deployment means…
choices: The new model scores live traffic in parallel without affecting decisions, for comparison

cards.q: What is a trace, and why is it the unit of LLM debugging?
cards.answer: A trace is the full record of one request: user input, prompts, retrieved context, every LLM and tool call (spans) with inputs/outputs, latency, tokens and cost, and the final output. LLM failures emerge from the whole chain, so you need the complete context to see where it went wrong (bad retrieval, wrong tool, bad generation). Traces are also what error analysis reads.
rubric: Full end-to-end record incl. intermediate steps
Failures arise across steps / need full context
Basis for error analysis and evals

cards.q: A 'span' within a trace is…
choices: One operation (an LLM call, retrieval or tool call) with its inputs, outputs and timing

cards.q: Why run evals in CI when a prompt changes?
choices: To catch regressions on known failure modes before deploying

cards.q: Key panels for an LLM production dashboard?
choices: Latency (p50/p95), cost per request, error/fallback rate, eval pass rates, user feedback
Number of prompts in the repo

cards.q: Privacy concern with storing LLM traces in fintech?
choices: Traces may contain PII/financial data: redact, restrict access, and set retention limits

cards.q: Name three ways to cut LLM serving cost without changing the model.
cards.answer: Prompt/prefix caching; response caching for repeated queries; shorter prompts and context (trim retrieved chunks, compress history); batching requests; capping max output tokens; routing easy queries to cheaper paths; efficient serving engines (continuous batching, paged attention).
rubric: Any three of: caching, shorter context, batching, output limits, routing, efficient serving engine

cards.q: Continuous batching (e.g. in vLLM) improves throughput by…
choices: Adding/removing requests from the batch at each decoding step rather than waiting for the whole batch to finish

cards.q: PagedAttention addresses…
choices: KV-cache memory fragmentation by allocating it in fixed-size blocks

cards.q: Prompt caching helps most when…
choices: Many requests share a long identical prefix (system prompt, tools, documents)

cards.q: Speculative decoding speeds up generation by…
choices: A small draft model proposes tokens that the large model verifies in parallel
